scenario: On one operator-reported ESP-Mosaico V1.2 sample, boot kernel #36 in normal multiuser RAM mode and run the opt-in one-shot selected-peer RX observer during a WPA3/SAE profile with PMF required.
expected: The selected BSS passes vendor compatibility checks, SAE and the WPA four-way handshake complete with PMF, and the interface obtains an IP address for data exchange.
observed: Kernel #36 booted through ROM, firmware, kernel and the existing RAM root to normal multiuser init, getty and root login; the NOR and root were unchanged. The supplicant reported SAE/association status 0 and accepted=1 with profile authmode 9; EmberBSD published RUN with joined=1 and link=1. Callback counters recorded mgmt=372 and data=88, with bad and short counters zero. Among valid DATA headers, all_data=88, selected-TA ap_data=8 and FromDS ap_downlink=8; the association response was addressed to this station (assoc_self=1, assoc_other=0). Before restore, current promiscuous mode=1/result=0 and filter=0x5/result=0. The selected-peer observer counted 116 management frames; the strict own-DA data counter and EAPOL counter were zero. Restore calls returned 0/0/0. About ten seconds later the vendor reported reason 204 and the supplicant timed out and locally disconnected. No WPA_COMPLETED, negotiated PMF, IP address, DNS or accepted network data exchange was observed. These callback counters establish that DATA reached the callback, but do not establish that M1 was absent over the air or that the AP or radio is defective.
limits: One operator-reported V1.2 sample and RAM-only trial; this does not establish another board revision or persistent installation.
The RAM root is identified by role only; its private configuration is not part of this shared record.
Observed times are kernel uptime; the full capture duration is not established. The private capture and its path are not part of this shared record.

The receive observer is opt-in and can affect timing. Its ESP-IDF promiscuous callback and filters only report successful RX frames; the data count additionally requires FromDS direction and receiver address equal to this station. These counters do not establish that the AP sent or did not send frames outside the observer's visibility.

The observer's own-DA data and EAPOL counters were zero even though DATA reached the callback; the data counts have different address/direction filters. The capture does not establish that M1 was absent over the air or identify an AP/radio fault.
A WPA2 comparison did not reach BSS selection or association: wpa_cli was killed with status 137 during setup after out-of-swap. This is not a WPA2 authentication result.
No WPA_COMPLETED, negotiated PMF, IP address, DNS or accepted network data exchange was established. WPA2-only authentication, reconnect, roaming and sustained transfer remain unaccepted.
